terms.definition: The quantity whose unit is the mole, used to count particles.
terms.examiner: Write "amount of NaCl", not "amount of salt": OCR uses the formula of the substance.

terms.definition: The amount of substance that contains as many particles as there are atoms in exactly 12 g of carbon-12: 6.02 × 10²³ particles.
terms.examiner: Say what the particles are: atoms, molecules, ions or electrons.

terms.definition: The number of particles per mole, 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
terms.examiner: It is on the Data Sheet. Multiply moles by it to get particles; remember to multiply again if the question asks for atoms or ions in each formula unit.

terms.definition: The mass per mole of a substance, in g mol⁻¹.
terms.examiner: n = m ÷ M. Use the relative atomic masses from the Periodic Table as printed.

terms.definition: The volume per mole of a gas, in dm³ mol⁻¹: 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹ at room temperature and pressure.
terms.examiner: Only use 24.0 at RTP. At other conditions use pV = nRT with Pa, m³ and K.

terms.definition: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element present in a compound.
terms.examiner: Divide each mass or percentage by the relative atomic mass, then by the smallest answer. Do not round 1.5 or 1.33 to a whole number: multiply up.

terms.definition: The number and type of atoms of each element in a molecule.
terms.examiner: Molecular formula = empirical formula × (Mr ÷ empirical formula mass).

terms.definition: Water molecules that are part of the crystalline structure of a hydrated salt.
terms.examiner: Anhydrous means with no water of crystallisation. Heat to constant mass to be sure all the water has gone.

terms.definition: Actual amount of product ÷ theoretical amount of product × 100.
terms.examiner: Work in moles, and find the limiting reagent first.

terms.definition: Sum of the molar masses of the desired products ÷ sum of the molar masses of all products × 100.
terms.examiner: Use the balanced equation, including the balancing numbers. Addition reactions have 100% atom economy.
